text:
nora: Quick smoke help needed for customer CobaltField. They merged their adapter (cf-lora-2026-03) and after we applied int4 profile some invoice amounts are changing format or dropping cents. Can someone run a quick compat + int4 smoke? They attached a 28-example mini-pack.

tim: I'll grab it. Can you paste a few of the flagged lines?

nora: pasted three that failed in QA: 
- Invoice total: $4,750.50
- Factura total: 4.750,50 
- Charge: A4750.5
They say in some renders cents disappear or decimals round to .0 after merge+int4.

ara: kicking a short eval on host-test with rdx-base-3b quant=int4, adapter=cf-lora-2026-03. job id eval-1772468101-a. ETA ~6m.

eval-bot: queued eval-1772468101-a on runner-5 (est 5m).

tim: command used: 
```
redwood eval run --model rdx-base-3b --adapter cf-lora-2026-03 --quant int4 --tasks currency-format --samples 28 --out /tmp/cobalt-smoke.json
```

ara: quick top-level: PPL(base)=10.9, PPL(merged)=11.6 (+6.4%). Numeric format diffs 5/28, token-boundary diffs 3/28. One example where "4,750.50" tokenized as ["4", ",", "750", ".", "50"] -> merged produced a merged token that dropped ".50".

nora: any tokenizer mismatch? did they train with a different tokenization pipeline?

ar a: customer claims they used a custom preprocessor that normalizes spaces and uses a LocaleToken tag during training. Could be the adapter learned to emit the tag which our tokenizer doesn't expect.

merge-bot: diff-merge report attached: delta_tokens=8, delta_logits_small_shifts=6, noted high-norm adapter rows in layer 6. See /artifacts/eval-1772468101-a/diff.json

tim: re-run with tokenizer_v2 flag: PPL(merged,tokenizer_v2)=11.2 (delta +2.8%) and token diffs reduced to 1/28 (still the euro example). So tokenizer version reduces boundary issues but one lingering case.

nora: good. try int8 too to separate quant effect.

ara: int8 run queued -> PPL(merged,int8)=11.0 (delta +0.9%). Numeric diffs reduced to 2/28. So int4 amplifies the remaining mismatch.

tim: I inspected adapter delta magnitudes; a few rows >1.6 which could be causing precision-sensitive shifts after int4. Ran a quick clamp-merge (clip to [-0.7,0.7]) and re-ran int4 smoke locally: diffs down to 0/28, PPL penalty acceptable (~+1.5%). Script: 
```
# clamp merge
python tools/merge_adapter.py --adapter cf-lora-2026-03 --clip 0.7 --out merged-clamped.safetensors
```
I saved a temp gist: https://gist.github.com/temp/cf-clamp

nora: nice. Action items: 1) ask CobaltField for their tokenizer recipe and preproc (LocaleTag usage); 2) recommend they re-run training with tokenizer_v2 or include token remap; 3) offer clamp-merge as short-term mitigation; 4) add the 28 examples to onboarding-regress/cobaltfield.json labeled "currency-cents-drop".

ar a: also tried a remap pre-tokenize step that standardizes thousands separators to comma and normalizes decimal marker; that removed boundary diffs but didn't fix the cents-drop in all cases. So two separate vectors: tokenizer mismatch vs adapter-induced numeric bias.

tim: I'll draft a short runbook for numeric regressions on adapter merges (steps: compare int8/int4, check tokenizer variants, inspect adapter delta L2 norms, try clamp-merge, add failing examples to regress suite, request training seeds). Creating PR: https://git.redwood.internal/runbooks/pull/512

nora: pinging SE to request training artifacts from CobaltField and cc'ing product for visibility.

merge-bot: created ticket RW-78901 assigned eng-ml: "CobaltField adapter onboarding - tokenizer + int4 smoke".

nora: marking thread as "smoke -> investigating". Thanks for fast turnaround y'all :heart:
